newsitem.title: BOLIVIA: SOCCER-URUGUAY COME TO LIFE AGAINST VENEZUELA IN COPA AMERICA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-URUGUAY COME TO LIFE AGAINST VENEZUELA IN COPA AMERICA.

text.p: Defending champions Uruguay, who suffered a shock defeat to Peru in their opening Copa America game, came briefly to life Sunday as they beat Venezuela 2-0.
A brilliant individual goal by Alvaro Recoba in the first half put Uruguay on top after a sticky start against the competition's weakest team in a near-deserted stadium.
Marcelo Saralegui added a goal early in the second half to lift Uruguay into second place in group B, ahead of Peru on goal difference.

Uruguay have brought most of their regular internationals to the tournament, which has been devalued because it is being held in the middle of the region's World Cup qualifying matches. However, top names such as Enzo Francescoli are missing.
Venezuela are fielding their full-strength team as they have no chance of qualifying for next year's World Cup.

In the 25th minute, Recoba scored one of the best goals of the tournament when he picked up the ball on the edge of the penalty area and ran through a group of defenders before slotting the ball past goalkeeper Rafael Dudamel.
He nearly scored a second before halftime but saw his shot rebound off a post.
Venezuela twice came close to equalising before halftime but suffered after having Rodolfo Rodallega sent off for a foul in the 35th minute.

Saralegui scored from close range two minutes into the second half, which prompted Venezuela into their best spell of an otherwise dull match as they created a number of chances. In their best move, Juan Luis Socorro hit the post with a blistering 25-metre drive.
The game, played at 2,700 metres above sea level, petered out and the last quarter was played at walking pace as the teams appeared to feel the affects of the high altitude.

Uruguay - 1-Robert Siboldi, 2-Hector Rodriguez, 3-Eber Moas, 5-Gonzalo de los Santos, 6-Tony Gomez, 8-Marcelo Saralegui, 9-Luis Alberto Ramiro (22-Sebastian Abre, 60), 10-Alvaro Recoba (14-Clever Romero,70), 11-Javier Delgado, 15-Tabare Silva, 18-Ruben da Silva

Venezuela - 1-Rafael Dudamel, 3-Alexander Echenique, 4-Jose Manuel Rey, 5-Luis Valenilla, 6-Leo Gonzalez, 7-Juan Carlos Socorro, 8-Gerson Diaz, 9-Rafael Castellin, 10-Gabriel Miranda (18-Andrew Paez, 75), 17-Elvis Martinez, 20-Robert Rodallega.
